pillar_reactions.evidence: Arrived pre-sold on the modality and articulated the mechanism himself before the rep presented anything: 'rather than like a static, I'm just, you know, doing bicep curls to work the bicep. It's more of a, I'm working the full movement of the body, which quite honestly, I think is more what I need.' When mobility was framed as the neglected foundation he agreed flatly — 'Yep' — and tied it to his own desk-bound day. He also volunteered that his skating background makes him receptive: 'skating could probably be beneficial because my body remembers it.'

Understood and agreed with no friction and no questions. On the what/when/how-much frame: 'Yeah, no, I get it. Easy.' Asked directly whether he had questions on nutrition he said 'No.' He accepted the eight-hour window and the once-a-week flexibility without pushback. The rep's strongest move here was retrospective rather than persuasive — anchoring against his failed prior programme with 'we're not vShred, so we're not going to be dissecting cucumber', which drew 'that's a good thing.'

The pillar he bought on. He named the need before it was presented — 'that's what I think I need at this point, whether it's Trevor or somebody else' — and reacted strongly to the video form-check mechanic: 'very few, very few trainers do that... with the online.' The shame lever landed hardest: 'You can lie to Alexa, but it's going to be way difficult to lie to Trevor' drew 'Yeah, I know. And then, like I said, I'll be embarrassed and I'll do it.' He had already articulated the same thing unprompted: 'I would be beyond embarrassed if I let someone like Trevor down.'

anchors.raw: I saw that Trevor's got, like, just like a monthly membership thing where it's access to his exercises, not a one-on-one thing, but I'm like, you know what? Even that might not be a bad thing for me. It's better than what I'm doing now.
anchors.note: The most important anchor on the call and the rep never addressed it. The prospect had already priced a cheaper Primal Instinct product and told himself it would be acceptable, before the $6,000 was named. Nothing in the presentation distinguished the one-to-one programme from the membership beyond Trevor's personal involvement, and the rep did not ask what the membership costs or why one-to-one is worth the difference.

anchors.raw: I did hire vShred about a year ago, and they ended up not being what I thought they were going to be... I think I spent a lot of money for something that didn't give me what I thought I was getting.
anchors.note: A burned buyer, and it cuts toward the sale rather than against it: the specific failure he describes — no instruction, no form correction, three injuries — is exactly what the video form-check and weekly check-in are sold on. The rep used it well as a contrast ('we're not vShred'). He never asked what vShred cost, which would have given him the only real price reference point available on the call.

anchors.raw: I don't think any of mine have 6,000 available on it. I'll have to look.
anchors.note: Not a value objection — he said outright 'I don't have a problem with 6,000. It's just figuring out how to get it so I can do it all at once.' The constraint is instrument and liquidity, precisely what the open wallet exists to map, and it was left unmapped. Whether Monday's payment is real is unknown because no card, balance or surplus figure was ever taken.

anchors.raw: I'm less than a mile or, you know, just about a mile from the gym that's on post... I can use a gym for free because I'm an army and I have access to it. I can use it for free.
anchors.note: A free, walkable, fully equipped facility is his status quo. He undercuts it himself — the problem is that it is 85 machines with no plan — but it remains a standing zero-cost alternative that anyone selling him $6,000 of structure is implicitly competing against.

unmet_demand.want: To come off prescribed cholesterol medication and raise testosterone without hormone therapy — 'there's got to be a way where I can change my diet and my fitness structure where I shouldn't need these things in the future'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: This is a clinical outcome, not a fitness outcome, and the programme has no clinician in it. The rep did not decline it; he endorsed it — 'We want to quit that... it is possible to ditch that. Like, Trevor had those clients that they fixed their cholesterol' — which converted an unmet demand into a promise nobody can stand behind. The prospect left the call saying 'I refuse. I'm not doing it anymore.'

unmet_demand.want: Confirmation that a 52-year-old is genuinely inside the programme's target rather than an exception
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Trevor's own advertising states men aged 30-45. The answer he received from the team was a soft 'that range is generally the most people that are interested', and on this call the answer was an anecdote about a 69-year-old. He raised the doubt three separate times, including 'I think I need to do a little bit on my own to prove I'm worthy of Trevor.' The programme evidently serves this age group; the marketing says it does not.

unmet_demand.want: A training programme that will not re-injure him, given historic Achilles tendinitis, ongoing physical therapy and three injuries on his last online programme
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep's answer was the video form-check and 'the crucial thing is not to get injured'. That is a plausible answer and may well be sufficient, but it was never checked against his physical therapist and nobody asked whether loaded ballistic kettlebell work is appropriate for an Achilles under active rehabilitation. Unresolved rather than unserved.

unmet_demand.want: Help fixing chronic sleep-onset insomnia, which he named as terrible and has already had investigated with a sleep study
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Sleep is used as a weekly check-in metric and the rep offered a wind-down protocol, but sleep coaching is not one of the three pillars and was not part of the offer. He had already tried the obvious behavioural fixes himself. The programme probably does help indirectly via training and nutrition, and nobody said so clearly or claimed it as scope.
